Round 30: the removals

Visibility Atlas, 30 October 2026. Before is the published build (HEAD, 3b4a7cb); after is the working tree. Seven removals, each built as its own step: the region fill (F), the pulse's tree lines (R), BLINK (B), the light theme (T), the scrolling wire (W), the profile in the tile (P) and the RUSSIA controls (X), with the phone line collapsed by default (your pick). Nothing is committed: each step becomes its own commit after your approval.

Checks

Five-width audit (400, 768, 1,200, 1,600 and 2,000 px in one run): zero findings, 1,301 states (1,376 at round 29's gate; the removed features' states went with them).

Change proof against HEAD: all 44 frames at 1,600 px differ, as expected, in the header, the strip, the LAYER and GO TO cards (and the cards below them, which move up), the tile and the faint fill under the hover ring. The map changes nowhere else. 353 text groups differ: the wire's items, the guide, the header, the tips, the red button's label, the GO TO reading text and the REFERENCES type line. No new rule hits.

The film: 13 frames across the full cut are identical to HEAD's after the shared drawing code lost its light-theme branches.

Known tight spots, accepted with the phone pick: with the line opened on a phone, the right-hand column rises 24 px. With the revenue mix box also expanded, the scale bar meets the box by 3 px at the tallest phone map, and on the 375 by 667 and 360 by 800 phones the tile has no docking place while the line is open.

Found on the way and fixed: on a touch phone the collapsed line's stub overlapped the scale bar by 8 px, because the touch rule came before the phone rule in the stylesheet. It never showed while the line was open by default.

The whole page at 1,600 px

Cells view, Leading industry by year, 2024. The header loses LIGHT THEME, the strip shows one sentence in place of the scrolling wire, and the GO TO card loses RUSSIA and the minimap's corner brackets.

Firms view, 2024.

F · The hovered region's fill

Hovering Krasnoyarsk at the country view. Before, the region took a faint fuchsia fill under the data; after, only its outline. The map no longer redraws when the pointer crosses a region border.

R · The pulse's tree lines

The Firms view's pulse for 2022, 1.3 s into the sweep. Before, the minimum spanning tree traced behind the sweep; after, the firms still swell as the sweep passes, with no lines. The red button's label loses "Lines join them by distance only."

B · BLINK

The LAYER card. On Statement share by year the second line keeps the red button and its counter. On Pairs shared by 100+, which follows the slider but has no red button, that line held only BLINK, so it goes and the card is one line shorter. The B key does nothing now.

Statement share by year.

Pairs shared by 100+.

The Firms view.

T · The light theme

The header loses LIGHT THEME, and REFERENCES moves to the right edge. Returning viewers who had chosen light keep a key in their browser that the page no longer reads, and they see the dark page.

At 400 px.

W · The scrolling wire

The strip keeps its glyph and gives one sentence about the place under the camera: the round-9 line, which was the reduced-motion form. Tips still take its place once in a while when nothing moves. The cat facts, the anniversary lines, the named firms and the national facts went with the wire, and so did its glow and the Tomorrow face.

Hovering Kazan: the line follows the hovered region at once.

At 400 px (your pick): the line starts collapsed to its toggle, as the legend and the note do, so the map gains 34 px; opened, it takes two rows.

P · The profile leaves the tile

Hovering Moscow at the Moscow preset. Before, the tile ended with a box holding the profile's headline; after, the tile ends at its footer, and the profile shows in the UNDER THE CURSOR card only.

X · One way to fit the country

The GO TO card loses the RUSSIA button and the minimap's corner brackets, which were a button too, with the Diomede Islands fact as their tooltip. The zoom box's fit button and the 0 key fit the country, and a #Russia link still opens there.
